articles.headline: Socceroos transfer tracker: Where Australia's stars will play in 2026-27
articles.description: Transfer deadlines are hitting across the globe and, with it, bringing to an end a window that has seen a remarkable surge in interest in players who represented the Socceroos at the FIFA World Cup.

images.name: Alessandro Circati, Nestory Irankunda and Lucas Herrington [1295x729]
images.caption: Alessandro Circati, Nestory Irankunda and Lucas Herrington
images.alt: Alessandro Circati, Nestory Irankunda and Lucas Herrington

images.name: Mo Touré bags quickfire double for Norwich City
images.caption: Mo Touré explodes for two goals within the space of 20 minutes as Norwich City thrash Burnley 4-1 in the Championship.

articles.headline: Japan 'came here to win the World Cup, not fun' - Yukinari Sugawara
articles.description: Japan wingback Yukinari Sugawara has reiterated that his team are at the World Cup not just to participate, but to win it.

images.name: Yukinari Sugawara [1296x729]
images.caption: Japan's preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup saw them record first-ever wins over Brazil and England, following on from their huge upsets over Germany and Spain back in the 2022 edition of the tournament.
images.credit: John Walton/PA Images via Getty Images

images.name: How captain Endo's injury will force Japan to reshuffle
images.caption: How captain Endo's injury will force Japan to reshuffle

articles.headline: Tete Yengi credits journeyman career for World Cup call-up
articles.description: Socceroos bolter Tete Yengi says his journey to the national team has not been straightforward, but he believes these adventures have played a key role in his pursuit of becoming the "ultimate player" and, more importantly, a World Cup representative.

images.name: What are the expectations for Australia at the World Cup?
images.caption: Joey Lynch reacts to Australia's squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

articles.headline: Why Japan could be the most exciting team at the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.description: Even with a couple of key players out through injury, Japan could still be the most exciting team at the 2026 World Cup.

images.name: Japan [1296x729]
images.caption: Japan's preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup has seen them record victories over Brazil and England for the first time ever over the past seven months.

images.name: Kaoru Mitoma [1296x729]
images.caption: Japan were dealt a real blow ahead of the World Cup after injuy ruled out Kaoru Mitoma, who scored the only goal of the game when they beat England 1-0 at Wembley back in March.

images.name: Have injuries ruined Japan's chances of causing World Cup upsets?
images.caption: Gabe Tan reacts to Japan's squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

articles.headline: Tolgay Arslan's last chapter with Sanfrecce Hiroshima brought some final silverware, and a closing sense of fulfilment
articles.description: Tolgay Arslan has announced his retirement -- perhaps ending it all after a final sense of fulfilment at Sanfrecce Hiroshima.

images.name: Tolgay Arslan [1296x729]
images.caption: Sanfrecce Hiroshima star Tolgay Arslan announced his retirement on Wednesday following a storied career that also saw him play for Hamburg, Beşiktaş, Fenerbahçe, Udinese and Melbourne City.

images.name: Tolgay Arslan [1296x729]
images.caption: In his two years with Sanfrecce Hiroshima, Tolgay Arslan with lift silverware twice -- the Japanese Super Cup and J.League Cup, both in 2025.

articles.headline: Could this FIFA World Cup be Takefusa Kubo's time to shine for Japan?
articles.description: After a disappointing World Cup debut last time out, 2026 could just be Takefusa Kubo's time to shine for Japan.

images.name: Takefusa Kubo [1296x729]
images.caption: Still only 24, Takefusa Kubo is already the sixth-most capped member of the current Japan squad as he prepares to play at the FIFA World Cup for the second time.

images.name: Takefusa Kubo [1296x729]
images.caption: Takefusa Kubo had a difficult World Cup in 2022 as he was substituted at halftime in both of his appearances, and missed the round of 16 elimination at the hands of Croatia due to injury.

images.name: Kaoru Mitoma; Takefusa Kubo [1296x729]
images.caption: With Kaoru Mitoma ruled out of the World Cup alongside another key playmaker in Takumi Minamino, increased responsibility will now fall on Takefusa Kubo as Japan's playmaker-in-chief.

images.name: Have injuries ruined Japan's chances of causing World Cup upsets?
images.caption: Gabe Tan reacts to Japan's squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
